title: Stephen (Acts 6–7)
hook: the first to die for the faith, forgiving those who stoned him

segments.voice: Yesterday, the first community: teaching, fellowship, bread and prayers. Your line was they held all things in common. What did you give or lend? Day seventy-five.

Every community hits its first real argument, and the first Church's was about food. The Greek-speaking widows complained they were being overlooked when the daily meals were handed out. So the apostles asked the community to choose seven men to take charge of serving, and they laid hands on them. The first name on the list is Stephen. In the Douay-Rheims: "And Stephen, full of grace and fortitude, did great wonders and signs among the people." He's a man who serves tables, and he also can't stop talking about Jesus. Within a chapter, that gets him killed. Today's word is what the Church has called him ever since.
screen: `THE FIRST ARGUMENT: FOOD.` → `SEVEN CHOSEN TO SERVE.` → `FULL OF GRACE AND FORTITUDE.`

segments.voice: Some men from a synagogue in Jerusalem argue with Stephen and can't win, so they bring him before the council with charges against him. Luke says everyone looking at him saw his face like the face of an angel. He gives the longest speech in Acts, retelling Israel's whole story, from Abraham to Moses to the temple, and it ends hot. They're furious. And then Stephen looks up and says he sees the heavens opened and Jesus standing at God's right hand. They rush him, drag him outside the city and stone him. Luke adds a detail that will matter tomorrow: "the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man, whose name was Saul." Now listen to how Stephen dies. He prays: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit." Then he kneels and cries out: "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge." If those sound familiar, they should. They're the two things Jesus said on the cross: into thy hands, and forgive them. Stephen dies the way his teacher died. "And when he had said this, he fell asleep in the Lord." Martyr comes from the Greek martys, which meant a witness, the kind who testifies in court. Because so many early Christians testified with their lives, the word came to mean someone who dies for the faith. Stephen is called the first. The Church keeps his feast on December twenty-sixth, the day after Christmas, and Catholics trace the order of deacons back to him and the other six.
screen: `SEVEN TO SERVE, STEPHEN FIRST.` · `A FACE LIKE AN ANGEL.` · `HE DIES THE WAY JESUS DIED.` · `MARTYS: A WITNESS IN COURT.` · then, large: `LORD, LAY NOT THIS SIN TO THEIR CHARGE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: forgive one old hurt. Settle and breathe. Let a name come to mind, someone who hurt you, not the worst, just one that still stings. You don't have to pretend it didn't happen. Forgiving isn't saying it was fine. It's deciding not to keep holding the stone. Breathe out, and picture setting it down. If you pray, you can use Stephen's words for that person: Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. If today it's too much, it's enough to want to. The bell holds the time.
Martyr. From the Greek for a witness in court: someone who testifies with their life. Stephen was the first. Today's word.
Your line: lord, lay not this sin. Today, when someone wrongs you, even in something tiny, try not to add it to the pile. Day seventy-five.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Stephen, the first martyr, on 26 December, and ordain deacons, tracing their ministry of service back to Stephen and the seven.

original.note: Greek: a witness, someone who testifies. from it, martyr.

trapdoor: what you thought: a martyr is someone who dies for a cause.
what it means: a martyr is a witness, and Stephen witnessed to the end, forgiving the people who killed him.
what a scholar hears: martys was a courtroom word. Stephen's name, stephanos, means crown, and Luke shapes his death to mirror Jesus's in Luke 23.

notes: Douay-Rheims wording of Acts 6:8 and 7:57–59 given from memory; confirm. Verse numbering in Acts 7 differs by one between the Douay-Rheims/Vulgate and the KJV; confirm refs.
Framing: the script names 'men from a synagogue' and 'the council' as in Acts 6:9–12 and avoids any collective blame. Confirm it is careful enough.
Stephen's speech ends with sharp words (7:51–53); summarized as 'it ends hot'.
Martys: 'witness' in legal and general sense; the shift to 'one who dies for the faith' by the 2nd century. Confirm.
Catholic tradition traces the diaconate to Acts 6 (CCC 1571 area; Lumen Gentium 29). Some scholars question whether the seven were deacons in the later sense. Confirm phrasing.
Feast of Saint Stephen, 26 December (Latin Church; 27 December in some Eastern churches).
